marks.gloss_en: אביי דייק מרישא: טעמא דישראל עומד על גביו
Abaye, from the first clause: only when a Jew stands over him; if the Jew goes out and comes in, it is not permitted
רבא דייק מסיפא: טעמא דבא ומצאו ששחט
Rava, from the last clause: only where he came and found it already slaughtered is the test needed; if the Jew goes out and comes in, it is fine
דתניא: מצת כותי מותרת ... רבן שמעון בן גמליאל אומר: כל מצוה שהחזיקו בה כותים -- the baraita the claim cites (no SupportKind names a bare דתניא)
whether Kutim are relied on for an unwritten mitzva they embraced is a tannaitic dispute
אמרו ליה רבנן לרבא: תניא דמסייע לך -- the transgressors exchange their chametz: they do not leave the permitted (סברוה: R' Yehuda's view, Torah law)
the baraita: the chametz of transgressors after Pesach is permitted immediately, because they exchange it
ולאביי קשיא סיפא -- the last clause implies that exits-and-enters is permitted
אמר לך (on Abaye's behalf): יוצא ונכנס נמי בא ומצאו קרי ליה -- exits-and-enters is also called 'came and found'
ולרבא קשיא רישא -- the first clause implies that only standing over him permits
אמר לך (on Rava's behalf): יוצא ונכנס נמי כעומד על גביו דמי -- exits-and-enters is like standing over him
אמאי? ליחוש דלמא האי הוא דהוה שחיט שפיר -- perhaps the bird he eats is the one he slaughtered properly
במכניסן תחת כנפיו -- he does not know which bird he will be given (= p_menashe_machnisan)
Rav Menashe: the case is where the Jew tucks the birds under his wing, so the Kuti cannot know which he will be given
ודלמא סימנא הוה יהיב ליה בגויה? -- perhaps he marked the properly slaughtered one
דממסמס ליה מסמוסי -- the Jew mangles them, effacing any mark (= p_mesharshiya_memasmes)
Rav Mesharshiya: the Jew mangles the birds' necks, so any mark the Kuti left is effaced
ודלמא קסברי כותים אין שחיטה לעוף מן התורה? -- perhaps the Kuti eats an unslaughtered bird himself
ולטעמיך, שהייה דרסה חלדה הגרמה ועיקור מי כתיבן? אלא כיון דאחזיקו -- אחזיקו (= p_kevan_deachzuku)
are the five disqualifications of slaughter written in the Torah? rather, once the Kutim embraced them, they embraced them; here too, once they embraced bird slaughter, they embraced it
אי הכי, כי לא בדק נמי -- if he will not leave the permitted, why must one check the knife at all?
מיטרח לא טרח -- he will not trouble himself to check the knife
אי הכי, כל מצוה שהחזיקו בה כותים -- אם החזיקו מיבעי ליה! -- RSBG would have said 'IF they embraced'
R' Elazar forbids it, since they are not expert in the fine points of mitzvot like Jews
RSBG: every mitzva the Kutim embraced, they are far more meticulous in than Jews
what the tanna kamma's clause teaches: the Kutim ARE expert in guarding matza from leavening
first proposal: the tanna kamma and RSBG differ over a written mitzva the Kutim did not embrace (tk: relied on since written; RSBG: only if embraced)
second proposal: they differ over an unwritten mitzva the Kutim did embrace
Rava: a Jewish apostate who eats carcasses for appetite -- one checks a knife and gives it to him, and it is permitted to eat of his slaughter
the reason: where both the permitted and the forbidden are available, he will not leave the permitted to eat the forbidden
